subject: MAP & evaluation sprint: hosting path, region choices, and kickoff
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Chris Bartlett <cbartlett@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: MAP & evaluation sprint: hosting path, region choices, and kickoff

Hi Chris —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (Lumen_MAP_v3.xlsx) that breaks the next 6 weeks into (1) a 2-week POC/eval sprint, (2) a canary production window, and (3) an operational handoff. The primary decision points we need to confirm now are:

- Hosting path for the POC: Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (reserved capacity + SLA), or Private (on-prem / VPC)
- Target region for the POC: us-east vs eu-west (affects latency and data residency)
- Any compliance constraints (PII, vault/KMS requirements) that would push toward Dedicated/Private

High-level recommendation from our side for the POC is: start on Hosted in us-east to get results quickly, then pivot to Dedicated for production if you need guaranteed throughput and data isolation. That said, if Lumen has strict residency or procurement windows, we can prioritize a Dedicated pilot instead.

Please review the attached MAP and the quick evaluation checklist (eval_checklist_v2.pdf). If you can confirm region preference and any hard compliance blockers by next Tue (2026-12-14), we can lock the sprint plan and send a SOW addendum.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm region + must-have compliance items (by 2026-12-14)
- We update MAP and cost estimate (attached: dedicated_cost_estimate.xlsx)
- Kickoff call to align on success criteria (schedule preferred date/time)

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Lumen_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), eval_checklist_v2.pdf (doc), dedicated_cost_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Chris Bartlett <cbartlett@lumenhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation sprint: hosting path, region choices, and kickoff

Tessa —

Appreciate the tight timeline and the clear MAP. A few quick questions from our side before we lock region: 

1) Compliance: We need to confirm what evidence you can provide for SOC 2 + encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated and Private options. Is that a separate package?

2) Procurement: Our procurement team typically needs 6–8 weeks to sign a reserved capacity contract. If we start on Hosted for the POC, will that create any migration friction to Dedicated later?

3) Latency: If we run the POC in us-east, will eu users see degraded performance? We have a pilot group in London.

If you can answer the above, we’ll aim to confirm region and compliance blockers by Tues. Also looping our Security lead Priya Rao (cc).

Thanks,
Chris Bartlett
Head of AI Integrations
LumenHealth
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Chris Bartlett <cbartlett@lumenhealth.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation sprint: hosting path, region choices, and kickoff

Chris —

Quick answers to your questions:

1) Compliance evidence: We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and a KMS integration guide for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have documented encryption and tenancy controls; customer-managed keys are available on Dedicated/Private. I’ve attached a short cost/export note (dedicated_cost_estimate.xlsx) with the procurement cadence options.

2) Procurement & migration: Starting on Hosted is common and low-friction — our runtime supports model pinning and identical APIs across modes so migrating to Dedicated is mostly configuration + capacity reservation. The main work items are network/EKS/VPC peering for Private or KMS setup for Dedicated. We typically budget 2–4 weeks for migration prep if procurement is in flight.

3) Latency: us-east for the POC will be fine for prototype work; eu testers may see an extra 80–120ms roundtrip depending on routing. We can enable a lightweight region routing test during the POC to measure real numbers.

If Lumen’s procurement timeline forces a Dedicated pilot, we can start a 60-day reserved pilot at reduced commit to accelerate production readiness.

Ava — can you attach the routing/latency runbook and the brief KMS checklist to the MAP? Marissa — please add the canary rollout milestones to the spreadsheet so we have clear go/no-go gates.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dedicated_cost_estimate.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Chris Bartlett <cbartlett@lumenhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation sprint: hosting path, region choices, and kickoff

Chris —

Thanks for raising the questions. I updated the MAP (attached) and added an explicit canary rollout checklist and go/no-go criteria in tab 3. Summary of changes and recommendations: 

- POC recommendation: Hosted in us-east for rapid validation (target 2-week sprint).
- Canary plan: 1 week in us-east + a cross-region perf test from eu-west to validate latency impact. Go/no-go gate defined: SLOs (p95 < 250ms for core requests), no data residency violations, and successful KMS test if customer-managed keys are required.
- Dedicated pilot option: 60-day reserved pool with agreed-upon commit; procurement lead time expected ~6 weeks but pilot can start earlier with a reduced commit.
- Private (on-prem) path: feasible but requires additional work (networking, audit, on-site ops) — treated as a fallback for strict-regulated workloads.

I also attached the evaluation checklist (eval_checklist_v2.pdf) with test prompts and sample traffic patterns. If Lumen confirms Hosted/us-east for the POC, we’ll schedule the kickoff and circulate the detailed day-by-day calendar.

Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Lumen_MAP_v3.xlsx (updated), eval_checklist_v2.pdf
From: Chris Bartlett <cbartlett@lumenhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <prao@lumenhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation sprint: hosting path, region choices, and kickoff

Tessa / team —

We reviewed the updated MAP and the checklist with our Security and Procurement teams. Decision summary: 

- POC: Hosted in us-east (as proposed) — this lets our product team validate integration quickly.
- Production: Target Dedicated in us-east with customer-managed KMS; procurement will begin in Jan, with expected completion in ~6–8 weeks.
- Canary: We want the cross-region perf test during the POC before the canary window to set baseline numbers.

Actions:
- Please prepare a 1-page SOW addendum for Hosted POC (we will e-sign) and include the cross-region perf test as a required deliverable.
- Send available kickoff slots on Wed/Thu next week for a 60-minute alignment call.

Thanks to everyone for the quick turnaround. Looking forward to kicking this off.

Best,
Chris Bartlett
Head of AI Integrations
LumenHealth
